A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLPM research. All 23 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Existing appendix content can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original moderation experiments, output-steering evaluations, scaling studies, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds multimodal, multiclass, hybrid-model, checkpoint, latency, and baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: The per-layer GDA classifiers, shared covariance, last-token representations, and sparse aggregation procedure remain unchanged. v4 describes the VLM application as requiring no modifications. Its multiclass evaluation does not document an algorithmic revision; class-general prototype definitions already appear in v3.

E1.justification: v4 adds vision-language safety evaluation on HoliSafe and a 15-class WildGuardMix task distinguishing one safe and fourteen unsafe categories. These expand modality and classification requirements beyond v3's binary text moderation. The original eight harmfulness and seven neutral datasets remain.

E2.justification: Appendices O and P add focused comparisons against evaluation-selected best-layer GDA and a prompting-based LLM-as-a-Judge baseline. Existing comparator sets remain. HoliSafe and Nemotron experiments reuse Ayub and Majumdar and Abdelnabi et al., rather than introducing additional named comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate VLM and hybrid backbones, intermediate OLMo2 checkpoints, multiclass accuracy and AUROC, and latency across batch sizes 1–8, sequence lengths 256–1024, and different layer counts. Additional controls select the best GDA layer using evaluation performance and report average/best results across ten judge prompts. Existing experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds analyses of safety-feature development during training, SSM versus attention-layer contributions, measured latency under varying configurations, and MLPM versus an optimistically selected single layer. These address additional questions beyond v3's retained layer curves, component ablations, data scaling, generalization, and error analysis.

E5.justification: Table 17 adds explicit mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for execution times. The existing statement that nondeterministic methods are averaged over five runs remains unchanged. v4 does not specify the timing repetition count or establish an increase in classification runs.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables retain their values, while substantial new results appear. Examples include HoliSafe F1 scores of 0.923 and 0.957, multiclass accuracies of 0.6527–0.6659, and mean MLPM execution times of 0.134–0.828 ms. Hybrid, checkpoint, and new baseline results are also added. Unexplained MLPM score discrepancies in Tables 19–20 do not establish same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: The prototype and GDA definitions, aggregation equation, and computational and memory derivations in Section 3 and Appendix L are retained. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient, customizable, model-agnostic moderation, strong benchmark performance, and integration with output steering. The added experiments support these claims without materially rewriting their scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of early safety-feature development and later pretraining saturation, attributes a substantial benefit to SFT, and identifies SSM layers as the dominant hybrid-model contributors. It also interprets multimodal and multiclass results as broader applicability. The existing limitations concerning backbone quality and input moderation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 22 provides specific OLMo2 checkpoint identifiers, steps, and token counts, while Appendix M documents profiling configurations. The code-access disclosure and original implementation description remain. Detailed timing hardware and the ten judge-prompt templates are not supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds HoliSafe by Lee et al. (2025b) to support its vision-language evaluation. The existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged. Renaming the earlier Lee citation to 2025a is citation disambiguation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v4 inserts experimental subsections and Appendices M–R, adds acknowledgements and an author-contributions statement, updates affiliations and publication text, and makes limited wording and heading edits. There is no extensive rewrite of the original narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds the checkpoint plot in Figure 6, multimodal and hybrid comparison Tables 5–6, and supplementary Tables 17–22 covering distinct evaluations and analyses. Figure 4 is enlarged with revised axis ticks. Table 4 moves, and existing appendix displays are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Measured latency supplements v3's analytical efficiency estimates, the best-layer control tests aggregation more directly, and multimodal/multiclass results broaden validation. These provide a modest net benefit. Sparse experimental details and new inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 20 assigns Llama/Mistral MLPM scores opposite to Tables 2 and 19, and Section 4.5's checkpoint numbers disagree with Table 22.
